key_insight: No single flow surrogate architecture is universally best: the optimal choice depends on whether the dynamics are boundary-driven or self-sustained, and on how time dependence is handled.
engineering_relevance: For process and flow simulation, this means surrogate selection should be tied to the physics of the regime, because the wrong temporal model can miss the quantities engineers actually care about even if pointwise error looks good.
method: Compared 8 surrogate models on two transient flows: a 3D CMP slurry film and a 2D Kármán vortex street.
Evaluated models under a shared pipeline spanning full-field vs latent representations and one-shot vs autoregressive prediction.
Judged performance with five physics-oriented metrics: field, structure, invented motion, amplitude, and timing.
evidence_signal: A one-shot full-field model achieved 3.2% relative error on CMP wall-shear stress, while a latent autoregressive DeepONet preserved 96% of wake shedding power on KVS; all surrogates were 10^3–10^4× faster than the FEM solver.
watch_item: Low pointwise RMSE can be misleading, and the offline training-simulation cost must be included because the break-even point differs by regime.
paper_title: No Free Lunch in Flow Surrogates under Time-Varying Boundary Conditions: A Two-Regime Study
